narrative.overview: The sites look like equipment signage: a deep steel-navy bar across the top, signal amber where something needs attention, and plain dark-on-white text on a clean page. There is no decoration for its own sake. Real product photos and real numbers carry the visual weight, and the type is the operating system's own font. Amber reads as an andon or warning lamp, and the navy echoes the blue motors in the hero photo.
keyCharacteristics: Steel-navy header, hero and footer bands framing a light content area
One accent, signal amber, with dark ink text on it
System font stack, bold headings, regular body, no display face
Flat cards with a 1px hairline border and a 10px corner; shadows only on photos and video
Light and dark themes through prefers-color-scheme
Loud yellow placeholders so unfinished copy cannot ship by accident

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Amber is the only accent. It marks actions and counted or chosen things, not decoration.

rules.name: The Dark-on-Amber Rule
rules.body: Text on amber is Ink Navy. White on amber fails contrast.

rules.name: The Loud Placeholder Rule
rules.body: Unfinished copy is pale yellow. A page with any yellow like that on it is not ready to publish.

rules.name: The No-Web-Font Rule
rules.body: The system stack is a constraint of the current design, not an oversight. Changing it is a deliberate redesign decision.

rules.name: The Flat-Cards Rule
rules.body: Cards are outlined, not lifted. Shadows belong to photos and video.

dos: Do keep amber for actions and counted or chosen things (buttons, steps, featured option), with Ink Navy text on it.
Do use the system font stack and bold weights for hierarchy.
Do show real product photos and screenshots with the existing border, corner and shadow.
Do alternate white and mist sections, keep 56px section padding, and keep sections on the shared 1240px container.
Do keep both light and dark themes working (they use the same variables).
Do make unfinished copy pale yellow (.ph, .draft-banner) so it is obvious.
donts: Don't put white text on amber; it fails contrast.
Don't add a second accent color or decorative gradients; the only gradient is the navy hero.
Don't put shadows on cards. They belong to photos and video.
Don't introduce web fonts without treating it as a redesign decision.
Don't add stock photography, invented logos, customer names or testimonials. PRODUCT.md says none exist.
Don't let the two sites' CSS drift further apart without deciding whether they should share one file.
